about: The stage's story, as data (stage/stage.js reads it). One scene tells one story; each step adds one thing and is cumulative. From Dinis's arc to storytelling.1 (12 Nov 2026, 01:18 UTC): the five altitudes; the same privileges; policies; runs that cannot reach the asset; the mesh against one agent per asset; scale; cost. Numbers come from the run files; scenes on sim: graphs are labelled SIMULATED on screen. storytelling.1 and swarm.1.designer may edit this file: keys are documented in stage/README.md.

scenes.title: One agent, five altitudes
scenes.say: A real run from last night: one agent doing six of the storm site's scheduled jobs. Watch what one agent turns into.

steps.label: you and the agent
steps.caption: You ask one agent (A3) to do a job. It has memory, tools and its own wake.

steps.label: loops
steps.caption: It starts loops (A2): read, ask, check, retry. Six of them, one per job.

steps.label: model calls
steps.caption: Each loop calls a model (A1): one prompt in, one answer out. Eight calls, on OpenRouter.

steps.label: code
steps.caption: And code runs (A0): it reads the public storm data. 30 units from one request.

steps.label: by colour
steps.caption: Five altitudes, one colour each. The same job; very different powers needed at each level.

scenes.title: A swarm of loops
scenes.say: The same shape, bigger: 12 jobs on 4 models, 48 loops at once. Replayed from the run file, as it happened.

steps.label: the agent
steps.caption: Still one agent.

steps.label: the run, replayed
steps.caption: It fans out: 48 loops, 73 model calls, 96 units at once.

steps.label: who did the work
steps.caption: The agent did almost none of the work. Loops, calls and code did.

scenes.title: Everybody can reach everything
scenes.say: Today, everything an agent starts runs with the agent's privileges. Connect the agent to your systems and see who can reach them.

steps.label: the run
steps.caption: The same run: one agent, its loops, its calls, its code.

steps.label: connect the agent
steps.caption: The agent is connected: Gmail, Drive, GitHub, a database (the assets are simulated).

steps.label: who can reach them?
steps.caption: Who can reach them? Every loop, every model call, every line of code. Everybody.

steps.label: one goes wrong
steps.caption: One bad read, one prompt injection in the data: that code holds the agent's keys.

scenes.title: A policy on every unit
scenes.say: RiskMandate puts a policy on each unit: what it may reach, at its altitude.

steps.label: everybody
steps.caption: Where we were: everybody reaches everything.

steps.label: policy on
steps.caption: Policy on: only the agent may reach the assets. Loops, calls and code may not.

steps.label: but who enforces it?
steps.caption: But if the agent enforces its own policy, we are still hoping it behaves.

scenes.title: Run it where the assets are not
scenes.say: A real run from tonight. The agent only commits a signed request; a GitHub Action runs the loops; OpenRouter runs the calls. Neither is connected to your assets.

steps.label: a signed request
steps.caption: The agent commits a signed request. That is all it does.

steps.label: the push starts an Action
steps.caption: The push starts a GitHub Action: a different place, with no access to your systems.

steps.label: the work runs there
steps.caption: 36 model calls and 24 loops run there, and on OpenRouter.

steps.label: can they reach the assets?
steps.caption: Can any of them reach Gmail? No: they run where it is not connected. Not a policy: physics.

scenes.title: Five agents, every one wired to everything
scenes.say: People struggle with five agents, ten agents. Why: it is a mesh. Every agent has every connector.

steps.label: five agents
steps.caption: Five agents. A normal team setup.

steps.label: every connector
steps.caption: Each one has Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Slack, Zapier, GitHub, a database.

steps.label: one loses control
steps.caption: Any one of them can lose control, or make a mistake: and it reaches everything.

scenes.title: One agent per asset
scenes.say: With agentic policies: one agent may touch the inbox, one may touch the code, one may touch the database.

steps.label: the same five
steps.caption: The same five agents.

steps.label: one each
steps.caption: Each system has one agent allowed to reach it.

steps.label: one loses control
steps.caption: Agent 3 loses control: it reaches what it was given, and nothing else.

scenes.title: One push, twelve jobs at once
scenes.say: Because the work runs as small, isolated units, it scales. Tonight's scale test: one push, twelve GitHub jobs at once, every result signed.

steps.label: one job
steps.caption: One of the jobs: a signed request, an Action, its loops and calls.

steps.label: jobs at once

counter.label: GitHub jobs at once, from one push

steps.caption: Twelve of them at once, from one push.

steps.label: calls

counter.label: model calls from pushes, all of tonight

steps.caption: Every call recorded: model, tokens, cost, valid or not. Never the text.

steps.label: signed

counter.label: results, each signed and attested by GitHub

steps.caption: Each result signed by a key that lived only for its run, and attested by GitHub.

scenes.title: The same tokens, four prices
scenes.say: The big run again (73 calls, 236k tokens). What it cost, and what the same tokens would cost on each Claude model.

steps.label: Opus
steps.caption: Every unit on the top model: the most capable, the most expensive.

steps.label: Sonnet
steps.caption: Half of it on the middle model.

steps.label: Haiku
steps.caption: A twentieth of that on the small one.

steps.label: OpenRouter
steps.caption: What we paid: open-weight models on OpenRouter, for the loops that do not need the agent's brain.
